case.label: A
case.text: A is the smallest change (one edit to one existing SCP), so a candidate who reads only 'LEAST operational overhead' could pick it; it is ruled out only by the explicit constraint that every other Workloads account must keep the current allow list, which the stem states clearly. D fails because an SCP at the account level cannot grant what the OU allow list does not allow, and C is a migration. One honest gap in B: moving the account out of the Workloads OU also removes any other policies attached to that OU (for example deny SCPs or tag policies), but the stem names no such policies, so B stays the only answer. No wording cue gives B away: it is not the only option that adds Athena and AWS Glue (A and D do too).

case.label: B
case.text: In AWS Control Tower language a proactive control blocks a noncompliant resource before it is created, so a candidate could read B as 'prevent'. B fails because proactive controls are CloudFormation hooks and the stem says developers also change resources with the console and the CLI, which do not go through CloudFormation. C only reports after the event, which the stem rules out ('an alert after a deletion is not enough'). D works but attaching the same SCP to every account is more overhead than one OU attachment, and new accounts would need it again. Possible missing constraints that do not change the key: an SCP does not limit service-linked roles, and the stem does not say how many SCPs are already attached to the OU (the per-target SCP quota). Wording cue: A and D are near twins that differ only in the attachment target, which tells a test-wise candidate that an SCP is the mechanism; the stem constraint 'console and CLI' still has to be read to reject B, so the cue does not give the whole answer away.
